facts: The paper 'Stress‐Testing the “Universities Without Walls” Vision 2030: Lessons From Displaced Ukrainian Universities in Wartime' was authored by Marek Kwiek, Taras Finikov, Igor Lyman, and Yana Suchikova, and published in Higher Education Quarterly on 2026-11-02 (doi:10.1111/hequ.70186).

The study assesses the applicability and analytical sufficiency of the European University Association's (EUA) 'Universities Without Walls: A Vision for 2030' using displaced Ukrainian universities during Russia's full-scale invasion as critical empirical cases.
The empirical basis is a comprehensive audit conducted in 2024–2025 covering all 21 relocated Ukrainian universities that were operating predominantly online at the time.

The data collection methodology combined official and institutional data, open-source monitoring, visits to new locations, 21 group interviews with 179 members of university management teams, analysis of strategies, missions, and visions, and SciVal bibliometric indicators.
The findings demonstrate substantial but incomplete alignment between the practices of relocated Ukrainian universities and the EUA Vision 2030 framework.
The Vision 2030 framework productively captures openness, organisational flexibility, transnational collaboration, societal engagement, and autonomy.

The framework exhibits limitations when universities operate without a stable campus under prolonged security constraints, necessitating adaptations in quality assurance and academic community support.
The observed alignment between Ukrainian universities and Vision 2030 reflects survival practices developed in response to displacement rather than deliberate adoption of the EUA framework.
